The Nanomedicine Lab is also an affiliate member of the Centre for Nanotechnology in Medicine at the Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health of the University of Manchester in the United Kingdom which is fostering expertise and knowledge in innovative nanotechnologies for a broad range of medical applications.

The Nanomedicine Lab research portfolio includes the discovery and preclinical development of nanomedicine constructs based on novel, advanced nanomaterials of synthetic and biological nature. Great emphasis is placed at the interplay between in vitro and in vivo studies and how rationally designed and engineered nanoscale platforms can be safely translated into clinically effective therapeutics and diagnostics, with a particular interest in oncology and neurology.

Name: Marine NanoTech
Description:
Marine NanoTech specialise in the high quality restoration, renewal and protection of paint/gelcoat, glass surfaces and more for the Marine Industry. All products and processes are based on nano technology. 

The cutting-edge technology of our products and processes is designed in-house and exclusively for the marine industry, where Superyachts need the highest standards of quality, facing extreme challenging conditions, such as extreme sun exposure, salt, chemicals and abrasion on a daily basis. 

Marine NanoTech offers full flexibility around the busy itineraries in the yachting industry. MNT works globally, all services can be performed whilst the yacht is still in the water, no tenting is necessary.

The result is a gently renewed surface with a high shine, which is then sealed (optionally) and frozen in time with our highly formulated protective coatings ULTRA SHINE ARMOR and CERAMIC ARMOR.

We add to restore, we add to protect and we add long term value. 

We stand behind our technology- this is why we offer long term global warranty programs (12 months / 24 months / 5 years).

Name: shinephi
Description:
shinephi is a deep-tech company redefining how nanoscale processes are monitored and controlled — recently recognized as Catalan Startup of the Year 2025.

In both R&D and advanced manufacturing, critical nanoscale changes often go unseen. Traditional characterization forces a trade-off between speed and resolution, while production inspection is frequently offline, revealing defects only after a full batch is complete. The result: lost yield, wasted material, and delayed process optimization.

shinephi’s Solution — Real-Time Nanoscale Metrology, Built Into Your Tools
shinephi delivers a compact, modular imaging add-on that transforms standard optical microscopes into high-stability, high-sensitivity metrology systems:
• Real-time acquisition — up to 50 fps for fast characterization
• Sub-nanometric phase sensitivity — mapping topography and refractive index changes down to 0.1 nm
• Non-destructive 3D inspection — internal gradients and geometries without damaging samples
Built for Modern Nanofabrication

We help research labs, manufacturers, and equipment integrators:
 Reduce scrap and rework with in-process nanoscale inspection
  Preserve material value with fully non-destructive verification
  Monitor invisible transformations — from polymer curing to laser modifications — as they happen

Name: SOLARUP - EU HORIZON EIC 2021 PATHFINDER OPEN
Description:
SOLARUP directly addresses the ever louder call for sustainable energy production. The proposed solar energy conversion technology will reduce dependence on critical raw materials and overcome efficiency thresholds to unlock the future of flexible photovoltaic (PV) solar cells for mass deployment in smart buildings, soft robotics, wearable electronics, and other consumer products. Our main innovations lie in nanoengineering zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) for use as an earth-abundant direct bandgap semiconductor absorber and combined with a novel device architecture we target cell efficiency enhancements of up to 15%. Advanced manufacturing techniques such as nanoimprinting and metal-organic vapour-phase epitaxy will be explored to open industrially scalable routes to synthesise high quality Zn3P2 films. Moreover, our approach will allow reuse of the growth substrate, making sustainability another core element of SOLARUP’s radical vision. Optimisation of both the absorber structure and device architecture will be achieved through a holistic interplay of first-principles calculations and atomic scale structural and electronic characterisation.
The main outcome of SOLARUP will be the demonstration of an ultrathin-film PV technology that is scalable, cost-effective, and environmentally sustainable, complete with a comprehensive life cycle analysis. In this sense our aim is to feed and inspire the development of Zn3P2-based solar cells towards a market ready technology. The project consortium unites six European teams with complementary expertise at the forefront of Zn3P2 research, device architecture, and life cycle analysis, who will approach the ambitious challenges from a flexible and interdisciplinary perspective. SOLARUP has clear potential to make science-based contributions to energy security and high- quality job creation, while also connecting to industry and boosting the trajectories of early-career team members.

Description: The Advanced Electronic Materials and Devices group aims to explore fundamental electronic and electrochemical phenomena of novel materials, with a current particular emphasis on graphene and other 2D materials (e.g. MoS2), and to develop the fabrication and processing technologies necessary to prepare advanced electronic devices and systems based on them. Description:
Expertos en inspección, metrología óptica de precisión 2D/3D, microscopía electrónica y tomografía computerizada Distribuidores certificados de TESCAN, Bruker ALICONA y AshVision en España y Portugal.

Con la tecnología de Bruker ALICONA nos focalizamos en metrología óptica 3D (sin contacto) para verificación de piezas tanto en laboratorio como en entornos de producción. Medimos forma, tamaño, posición y rugosidad en superficies e interiores, incluso en miniaturizaciones complejas. Con la tecnología de TESCAN proporcionamos soluciones para el microanálisis con microscopia electrónica y tomografía de rayos X. Aplicables al control de calidad industrial, análisis forense, ciencia de materiales. Microscopios electrónicos para ciencias de la vida y aplicaciones biomédicas 2D y 3D. Description: We are an interdisciplinary group with diverse research interests. The N&N Group’s research is mainly focused on the rational synthesis of nanoparticles and nanocomposites and the study of their structural-functional properties including those related to the nano/bio interfaces. Name: GOTL (Optoelectronic and Laser Technology Group)
Description:
GOTL, fundado en 1994, es un grupo de investigación vinculado a la Universidad Carlos III de Madrid especializado en fotónica integrada aplicada a sistemas de microondas, ondas milimétricas y terahercios. El grupo desarrolla tecnologías avanzadas basadas en la convergencia entre fotónica y radiofrecuencia para aplicaciones en comunicaciones inalámbricas de banda ancha, sensado avanzado y plataformas espaciales.

 Líneas de investigación
Photonic Integrated Circuits (PIC): diseño y caracterización de chips fotónicos para la generación de portadoras RF en rangos de microondas, milimétrico y terahercios.
Procesamiento de señal RF en el dominio óptico: modulación, filtrado, multiplexación y demultiplexación para enlaces inalámbricos de banda ancha y sistemas de free-space optics.
Arrays de antenas integradas en milimétricas y terahercios: control fotónico de fase para beam steering y beam pointing de alta precisión.
Circuitos fotónicos integrados para cargas útiles satelitales: desarrollo de soluciones para plataformas espaciales, incluyendo aplicaciones en radiómetros.
Fotoacústica: diseño y desarrollo de sistemas láser de diodo para la generación de pulsos nanosegundo de  alta potencia mediante HPDL y controladores de alta corriente de pulso corto.

Con más de tres décadas de trayectoria, GOTL combina investigación fundamental y aplicada, participando en proyectos nacionales e internacionales y colaborando activamente con la industria tecnológica.

Description:
La sociedad actual se enfrenta a una serie de Retos cuyo objetivo es facilitar el crecimiento sostenible siendo respetuoso con el medioambiente que nos rodea. Para ello, es necesario trabajar en el desarrollo de nuevos materiales (nanomateriales) y nuevas tecnologías que aborden dichos retos.

- Recubrimientos funcionales basados en nanomateriales: propiedades de autolimpieza, hidrofóbicas, biocide, descontaminante, autorreparadores).

Ofrecemos también servicios de consultoría para empresas que quieran participar en proyectos del H2020:

- Gestión de proyectos

Name: 20th European Student Colloid Conference

Name: PERSEUS EU Project
Description:
PERSEUS is an EU-funded research project pioneering a nanotechnology-based cancer treatment for deep-seated, drug-resistant, and metastatic tumours.

Nanotechnology in cancer care is still in its infancy, but PERSEUS aims to bridge this gap with specially engineered nano-systems made of multifunctional 2D layered nanocrystals. Activated by X-rays, these nanosystems are designed to provide multimodal therapy with minimal side effects. Instead of killing cancer cells directly, CT scanner X-rays trigger and image the nanosystems, which locally produce non-mutagenic oncolytic effects.

This process converts low-energy CT X-rays into reactive oxygen species, radiosensitising agents, and heat; it can also induce immunogenic cell death, exposing or releasing neo-antigens that trigger an anti-cancer immune response. Unlike visible or near-infrared light-based therapies, X-rays can penetrate and treat deep-seated tumours. In short, CT radiation acts as the spark that lights the match – a radical vision for an ambitious, high-risk project.

PERSEUS targets multiple cancers, including metastatic triple negative breast cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The nanosystems are biocompatible and inactive without CT radiation: they only activate where the CT beam is delivered, minimising side effects at distal sites.

The therapy is agnostic with respect to tumour type and gender incidence, since it is not affected by patient biochemistry – a second paradigm shift. PERSEUS unites physicists, chemists, engineers, biologists, physicians, pharmacologists, and radiologists to deliver a transformative nanotechnological approach to urgent, unmet clinical needs.

Name: ANGSTROM_MERA
Description:
ANGSTROM: Plasma-Engineered Materials for Next-Generation Supercapacitors
ANGSTROM is a European research project tackling one of today’s biggest energy challenges: how to store power efficiently and sustainably. While batteries dominate the market, they face critical issues-scarcity of raw materials, safety risks, and limited lifespans. Supercapacitors offer fast charging and long durability, but their energy density needs a major boost.
Our solution? An eco-friendly plasma-enabled approach to design multifunctional hybrid electrodes. We combine Vertical Nanocarbon (VN) with Porous Active Materials (PAM) such as Covalent Organic Frameworks (COF) and highly conformal Porous Metal Oxides (PMO). This synergy will deliver high energy and power density, superior cycling stability, and pave the way for flexible, scalable devices.
The project moves from lab-scale concepts (TRL3) to industrial prototypes (TRL6), validating performance under real conditions and exploring commercialization. Applications range from electric vehicles and smart grids to IoT and wearable electronics.
Our consortium brings together leading expertise:
•	CSIC (Spain) – Plasma synthesis and advanced metal oxides.
•	Jožef Stefan Institute (Slovenia) – Nanocarbon growth and surface engineering.
•	CEITEC (Czech Republic) – 3D printing and flexible electrode design.
•	IQS nano (Czech Republic) – Industrial partner driving scale-up and prototyping.
ANGSTROM aligns with the EU Green Deal and Horizon Europe priorities, contributing to decarbonization and circular economy goals through sustainable, zero-waste processes.

Name: AMSwitch
Description:
AMSwitch is developing a new class of ultra‐low‐power logic switches using altermagnetic materials—an emerging magnetic state with zero net magnetization but electrically readable signals. These devices could operate below 1 aJ per bit, approaching fundamental energy limits.


The project explores two concepts: a gate‐tunable altermagnet switch using Berry‐curvature control, and a current‐driven switch that flips the altermagnetic order for compact logic operations. Together, they aim to enable reliable, non‐volatile, and energy‐efficient computing for future edge devices.


AMSwitch unites experts across materials science, nanoscale fabrication, device engineering, quantum theory, synchrotron characterization, and magnetometry—ensuring rapid progress from discovery to technology.


AMSwitch is coordinated by Chalmers University of Technology and has received funding from the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) under the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under Grant Agreement n° 101258102.

Name: Hybrid Materials and Surfaces Research Group
Description:
The Hybrid Materials and Surfaces (HMS) research group at the University of Jaén, part of the Andalusian research group ‘Molecular and Supported Metal Complexes of Biological or Technological Interest’ (FQM-273), is dedicated to the development of advanced functional materials through the integration of materials chemistry, nanotechnology, surface science, and polymer engineering.

The group has strong expertise in the design, synthesis, and characterization of hybrid carbon-based materials, including graphite, carbon black, MWCNTs, and GNPs, functionalized through innovative organic synthetic approaches. These strategies enable precise surface modifications that enhance properties critical for catalysis, energy conversion, and storage.

A core area of the group's research focuses on the production of polymers and polymer composites with tailored properties for biomedical and energy-related applications. This includes biocompatible materials, conductive polymers, and responsive systems. The group also actively integrates additive manufacturing technologies (3D printing) to fabricate custom-designed components and devices, offering flexible, scalable solutions for real-world applications in healthcare and sustainable energy.

Name: SmartCoDur Project
Description:
The SmartCoDur project aims to research and develop innovative solutions that contribute to increasing the durability of concrete structures reinforced with shape memory steel (Fe-SMA). The research focuses on the design of new smart and sustainable coatings that are capable of self-regulating and repairing themselves when their surface films are damaged.

This approach represents a promising alternative for significantly extending the useful life of infrastructure, reducing maintenance costs and minimising energy consumption throughout its life cycle. At the same time, SmartCoDur is aligned with the principles of sustainability and environmental respect, offering advanced technological solutions that respond to the current challenges of durability, efficiency and ecological responsibility in the construction sector.
